drillIntro: Walk the full repair flow on the fixed sample below: read the material, find the problem, rewrite the question, compare a suggested fix, then self-practice. Nothing touches real cards and no formal ratings are produced.
drillMaterial: TCP is a connection-oriented, reliable transport protocol. Both sides synchronise initial sequence numbers during the handshake and confirm each other can send and receive. Each step of the handshake confirms one specific thing.
drill2Material: Light travels at about 300,000 km per second in a vacuum. It slows in other media (about 3/4 of that in water). Any comparison of light speed must state the medium first.
drill2BrokenQ: What is the speed of light?
drill2Issue: Problem: a necessary condition is missing — light speed depends on the medium, so without stating one the question has no precise answer.
drill2Fixed: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
drill2Answer: About 300,000 km/s (299,792,458 m/s); slower in other media — roughly 3/4 of that in water.
drillMaterialNote: Source snapshot · version 2 · public practice material (edit freely)
drillIssue: Problem: the scope is far too broad — a “what is TCP” question can lead to definitions, handshakes, retransmission, teardown… The answer mixes many knowledge points, making recall heavy and mastery hard to judge.
drillEditNote: Edit above, preview the actual card below live. A good question asks exactly one clear thing and carries its necessary conditions.
drillFixedLabel: Fixed AI suggestion (local sample, no request)
drillFixed: When establishing a TCP connection, why must initial sequence numbers be synchronised?
drillCompareNote: Compare with your rewrite: does it also test exactly one thing, with conditions attached? There is more than one good fix — the bar is “answerable and judgeable”.
drillAnswer: Both sides exchange initial sequence numbers, progressively confirm each other can send and receive, and confirm the connection.
drillPracticeNote: Bypass practice performance never becomes real evidence — mastery is tracked by kernel scheduling and formal ratings.
drillFoot: Practice never enters real learning · no formal ratings · fixed sample, no model requests
